docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for the In-Dataset Discovery Service.

This service provides an API for natural-language exploration of structured and unstructured data in a dataset. It uses LLM-backed geospatial lookup and text-to-SQL. GET /explore runs the meteo text-to-SQL agent, which calls text2geo and then text-to-SQL. POST /text2sql4ap and POST /explore4ap write that SQL back onto an analytical pattern graph.

docs.text:

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text: The In-Dataset Discovery service exposes a RESTful API for performing in-dataset exploration operations, including geospatial queries, text-to-SQL conversion, and RAG-based question answering. POST /text2sql4ap and POST /explore4ap apply the same SQL result to an analytical pattern graph.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
The API is served from the root of the application. All endpoint paths are relative to the base URL where the service is deployed:

Base URL: https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/in-dataset-discovery/

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All operational endpoints require authentication except /health. See the Security page for more details.

docs.title: Text to Geospatial Objects Query
docs.text:
Performs geospatial queries using natural language to find locations, generate OverpassQL queries and return geospatial objects.

  • Endpoint: GET /text2geo
  • Description: Processes a natural language geospatial question, identifies the place using Wikidata, generates an OverpassQL query, and returns geospatial objects, resulting in coordinates, GeoJSON data, and bounding boxes.

  • Query Parameters:

    • question (required): The natural language geospatial query question.

  • Example Request: 

    GET /text2geo?question=What are the coordinates in Zurich?

  • Response Body (Success): 

    {
  "most_relevant_wikidata": {
    "place": "Zurich",
    "reasoning": "The question asks for the city of Zurich, which is best represented by the entity with ID Q72. This entity is described as the capital of the canton of Zurich and is a municipality and city in Switzerland. It also has 'found_osm_json: True', which gives it priority if multiple similar entities were found. Other entities like universities or sports clubs are not relevant to the context of the question, which specifically asks for the city.",
    "wiki_id": "Q72",
    "wiki_properties": {
      "aliases": "City of Zurich, ZH, Stadt Zürich, Zurich, Switzerland, Zürich",
      "coordinate location": "47.37444444444444, 8.54111111111111",
      "country": "Switzerland, Old Swiss Confederacy, Helvetic Republic, Switzerland",
      "description": "capital of the canton of Zurich, Switzerland",
      "found_osm_json": true,
      "instance of": "municipality of Switzerland, city of Switzerland, cantonal capital of Switzerland, college town, largest city, big city",
      "label": "Zurich",
      "located in the administrative territorial entity": "Zürich District",
      "part of": "Greater Zurich Area, Zurich metropolitan area, Canton of Zürich"
    }
  },
  "oql": {
    "OQL": "area[\"ISO3166-1\"=\"CH\"]->.searchArea;(nwr[\"wikidata\"=\"Q72\"];);",
    "reasoning": "Generated Overpass QL query using Wikidata ID Q72 and country ISO alpha-2 code CH."
  },
  "place": "zurich",
  "results": {
    "bounds": {
      "maxlat": 47.4346662,
      "maxlon": 8.6254413,
      "minlat": 47.3202187,
      "minlon": 8.4480061
    },
    "center": [
      47.4,
      8.5
    ],
    "geojson_data": {
      "features": [],
      "type": "FeatureCollection"
    },
    "points": [
      {
        "lat": "47.4",
        "lon": "8.5"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: results.points entries are { "lon", "lat" } strings, and results.center is [lat, lon]. A missing place returns 404. If Wikidata or Overpass cannot be reached, the response is 503. Other failures return 500. When LLM authentication fails, the client message can be "No place name found"; the log event is geospatial_place_name_extraction_failed. GET /explore and POST /explore4ap call this same step before text-to-SQL.

docs.title: Text-to-SQL Query
docs.text:
Converts natural language questions into SQL queries and executes them against a specified database.

  • Endpoint: POST /text2sql

  • Description: Takes a natural language question and database connection information, generates a SQL query using LLM capabilities, and executes it to return results. The parameters are:

    • db_info: The database connection information.
    • results: The results containing points for SQL query. The results parameter is optional. If not provided, the SQL query will be generated without parameters.
    • The db_info parameter is required. The db_info parameter is a dictionary with the following keys:
    • db_host: The database host.
    • db_username: The database username.
    • db_pass: The database password.
    • db_database: The database name.
    • db_schema: The database schema.
    • db_port: The database port.

  • Request Body with parameters:

    {
  "question": "What are the average mean temperatures in the coordinates (lon, lat) in year 2020?",
  "parameters": {
    "results": {
      "points": [[8.4, 47.4], [8.5, 47.4]]
    },
    "db_info": {
      "db_host": "the_db_host_ip",
      "db_username": "db_username",
      "db_pass": "db_password",
      "db_database": "database_name",
      "db_schema": "database_schema",
      "db_port": 5432
    }
  }
}

  • Response Body with parameters (Success):

    {
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Successfully generated SQL query on the first attempt.",
  "question": "What are the average mean temperatures...",
  "model_name": "gpt-4o",
  "sql_pattern": "SELECT AVG(tmean - 273.15)...",
  "sql_query": "SELECT AVG(tmean - 273.15) AS average_mean_temperature_celsius...",
  "sql_results": {
    "status": "success",
    "data": [{"average_mean_temperature_celsius": 10.5}]
  }
}

  • Request Body without parameters:

    {
  "question": "What are the average mean temperatures at lat 47.4, lon 8.4 in year 2020?",
  "parameters": {
    "db_info": {
      "db_host": "the_db_host_ip",
      "db_username": "db_username",
      "db_pass": "db_password",
      "db_database": "database_name",
      "db_schema": "database_schema",
      "db_port": 5432
    }
  }
}

  • Response Body without parameters (Success):

    {
"status": "success",
"message": "Successfully generated SQL query on the first attempt.",
"params": null,
"question": "Show the minimum temperature at lat 47.4, lon 8.5 in 2005",
"model_name": "gpt-4o",
"sql_pattern": null,
"input_params": null,
"output_params": null,
"reasoning": "The query is designed to find the minimum temperature recorded in the year 2005 at the specified latitude and longitude coordinates (47.4, 8.5). The temperatures in the 'meteo_tmin' table are stored in Kelvin, so they are converted to Celsius by subtracting 273.15. We use the WHERE clause to filter records that match the given coordinates and year, and then SELECT the MIN value of these converted temperatures.",
"sql_query": "SELECT MIN(tmin - 273.15) AS min_temp_celsius FROM era5_land2.meteo_tmin WHERE round(latitude::numeric, 1) = 47.4 AND round(longitude::numeric,1) = 8.5 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM time) = 2005;",
"sql_results": {
  "status": "success",
  "data": [
    {
      "min_temp_celsius": -12.898565673828102
    }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
The response keys above are unchanged. The default generator is DAIL-SQL (TEXT2SQL_FRAMEWORK=dail), one candidate at temperature 0. On that path the body matches the "without parameters" example: sql_pattern, input_params, and output_params are null even when results.points was sent. Clients use sql_query. model_name is the configured model (LLM_PROVIDER, default scayle, model SCAYLE_MODEL_NAME).

TEXT2SQL_FRAMEWORK=opensearch selects the OpenSearch-SQL graph. TEXT2SQL_LEGACY=true (or TEXT2SQL_PIPELINE=false) keeps the single-shot pattern path, which can fill sql_pattern, input_params, and output_params as in the "with parameters" example.

Coordinate pairs in results.points accept either order. When both values are within ±90, the larger magnitude is latitude, so [8.5, 47.5] and [47.5, 8.5] both resolve.

When db_database is era5land, generation uses METEO_DDL, UNIT_CONTRACTS (meteo_ssrd.ssrd is stored as J/m²), hints, the constraint validator, and a query rewrite. The table allowlist is landcover_upscaled, landcover_type, and meteo_*. Other databases use the live schema only. Few-shot text is taken from in-cluster Qdrant only when RETRIEVAL_ENABLED is on, the database is era5land, and retrieval returns text.

The query rewrite runs after SQL generation, and only for ERA5-Land. A coordinate predicate of the form ROUND(CAST(latitude ...), 1), ROUND(CAST(longitude ...), 1) IN ((...), ...) with 20 or more pairs is rewritten to IN (SELECT rlat, rlon FROM (VALUES ...) AS _geo_pts(rlat, rlon)). The coordinates are unchanged. PostgreSQL executes this VALUES join much faster, and its query optimizer does not apply the rewrite on its own. Lists with fewer than 20 pairs are left unchanged.

If generation or execution fails, the response can still be HTTP 200 with "status": "error" in the body. See the soft-failure note under Explore.

docs.title: Explore
docs.text:
Runs text2geo and then text-to-SQL for one natural-language question.

  • Endpoint: GET /explore
  • Authentication: Required.

  • Query Parameters:

    • question (required): The exploration question.

  • Example Request: 

    GET /explore?question=What is the average mean temperature in Zurich in 2020?

  • Response Body: Same keys as POST /text2sql (status, message, question, model_name, sql_pattern, input_params, output_params, reasoning, sql_query, sql_results), plus inference_time_s and db_fetch_time_s.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
The meteo text-to-SQL agent (meteo_agent) calls text2geo and then text-to-SQL. It uses the service ERA5-Land connection (DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME_ERA5LAND, DB_SCHEMA_ERA5LAND). The caller does not send db_info. On the default DAIL-SQL path, sql_pattern, input_params, and output_params are null. inference_time_s is total pipeline time minus database time.

A soft failure still returns HTTP 200. The body has "status": "error" when SQL generation fails, or sql_results.status of "error" when execution fails. The request was accepted, but the SQL step did not succeed. /explore logs meteo_agent_soft_failed. /text2sql logs text2sql_soft_failed. An unexpected exception is HTTP 500.

docs.title: Text-to-SQL for an analytical pattern
docs.text:
Generates SQL for the natural language operator (NLQ_Operator) already present on an analytical pattern graph.

  • Endpoint: POST /text2sql4ap
  • Authentication: Required.

  • Description: Accepts an analytical pattern graph (ap, with an Analytical_Pattern node) and returns the same graph enriched with the generated SQL, plus a metadata object that uses the POST /text2sql fields. metadata.sql_results is omitted. metadata.sql_query_with_args is set when the SQL names dataset tables.

  • Request Body: 

    {
  "ap": {
    "nodes": [],
    "edges": []
  }
}

The graph must include a natural language operator (NLQ_Operator), a relational-database node, its upstream dataset, and a database connection node.

  • Response Body (Success): 
    {
  "ap": {"nodes": [], "edges": []},
  "metadata": {
    "status": "success",
    "question": "Average mean temperature in 2020",
    "model_name": "Qwen3.8-Flash-Next",
    "sql_pattern": null,
    "input_params": null,
    "output_params": null,
    "sql_query": "SELECT ...",
    "sql_query_with_args": "SELECT ..."
  }
}

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The question is read from the natural language operator. Host, port, and database name come from the database connection node's contentUrl. Username and password are the service DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD (schema public). Generation is the same text-to-SQL path as POST /text2sql, with no caller-supplied points. On the default DAIL-SQL path, sql_pattern, input_params, and output_params are null. Prepared SQL is written onto the SQL operator, and dataset-table nodes are added for referenced tables. An invalid graph returns 422. DMM or database connection failures return 424.

docs.title: Explore for an analytical pattern
docs.text:
Runs the meteo text-to-SQL agent and writes the result back onto an analytical pattern graph.

  • Endpoint: POST /explore4ap
  • Authentication: Required.

  • Description: Same request body as POST /text2sql4ap. The response graph is enriched the same way. metadata keeps the GET /explore fields, including sql_results, inference_time_s, and db_fetch_time_s, and adds params.text2geo and params.text2sql.

  • Request Body: Same { "ap": { "nodes", "edges" } } body as POST /text2sql4ap.

  • Response Body (Success): 

    {
  "ap": {"nodes": [], "edges": []},
  "metadata": {
    "status": "success",
    "question": "Average mean temperature in Zurich in 2020",
    "sql_query": "SELECT ...",
    "sql_results": {"status": "success", "data": []},
    "inference_time_s": 4.2,
    "db_fetch_time_s": 0.8,
    "params": {
      "text2geo": {},
      "text2sql": {}
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The meteo text-to-SQL agent runs text2geo and then text-to-SQL, and writes the SQL onto the graph. Credentials come from the same source as POST /text2sql4ap. metadata.sql_results is kept. On the default DAIL-SQL path, sql_pattern, input_params, and output_params are null. An invalid graph returns 422. DMM or database connection failures return 424.

docs.title: Text Question Answer Query
docs.text:
Summarizes retrieved RAG context into an answer for a question.

  • Endpoint: POST /textQuestionAnswer
  • Description: Takes a natural language question together with retrieved RAG output and returns a short answer, a structured reason code, and the chunks used to produce the summary.

  • Authentication: Required.

  • Request Body: The request body must include question and rag_output. The rag_output object contains results and an optional query_time value.

  • Example Request: 

    {
  "question": "What is the chief town of the island of COPRAJA?",
  "rag_output": {
    "query_time": 3263.56,
    "results": [
      {
        "content": "COPRAJA, an island in the Mediterranean Sea... The chief town is Tratozzio.",
        "dataset_id": "d84d1a2e-127d-4393-91d0-afb7e4fd9c68",
        "object_id": "kp-eb0707-031203-1328-v2.xml",
        "similarity": 1.0
      }
    ]
  }
}

  • Response Body (Success): 

    {
  "answerable": true,
  "reason_code": "ANSWERED",
  "summary": "Based on the provided context, the chief town of COPRAJA is Tratozzio.",
  "used_chunks": [
    {
      "dataset_id": "d84d1a2e-127d-4393-91d0-afb7e4fd9c68",
      "object_id": "kp-eb0707-031203-1328-v2.xml",
      "similarity": 1.0
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: The In-Dataset Discovery Service is a self-contained application designed to act as a specialized query layer within the DataGEMS ecosystem.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
1. FastAPI Application: The heart of the service is a Python web application built with FastAPI. It exposes the REST API, handles incoming HTTP requests, and orchestrates all internal operations.

  2. Geospatial Component: A module that processes natural language geospatial queries, identifies places using Wikidata, generates OverpassQL queries, and retrieves geospatial data from OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API. GET /text2geo and the first step of GET /explore both use this module.

  3. Text-to-SQL Component: Converts a natural-language question into SQL and executes it. The default generator is DAIL-SQL (TEXT2SQL_FRAMEWORK=dail), with one candidate at temperature 0. TEXT2SQL_FRAMEWORK=opensearch selects the OpenSearch-SQL graph. TEXT2SQL_LEGACY=true (or TEXT2SQL_PIPELINE=false) keeps the single-shot pattern generator. On the DAIL-SQL path, sql_pattern, input_params, and output_params are null, and clients use sql_query. ERA5-Land receives METEO_DDL, UNIT_CONTRACTS, hints, the constraint validator, and a query rewrite. A ROUND(CAST(latitude/longitude)) IN (...) list of 20 or more pairs is rewritten as a VALUES join with the same coordinates. PostgreSQL executes that form much faster, and its query optimizer does not apply the rewrite automatically. Shorter lists are left unchanged. Other databases use the live schema only. Few-shot text comes from in-cluster Qdrant only when RETRIEVAL_ENABLED is on, the database is era5land, and retrieval returns text.

  4. Meteo text-to-SQL agent: GET /explore runs this LangGraph workflow (meteo_agent). It calls text2geo, then text-to-SQL, against the ERA5-Land database set by DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME_ERA5LAND, and DB_SCHEMA_ERA5LAND. POST /explore4ap runs the same chain and writes the result onto an analytical pattern graph, including metadata.params.text2geo and metadata.params.text2sql.

  5. Analytical-pattern-specific endpoints: POST /text2sql4ap and POST /explore4ap are the analytical-pattern-specific forms of /text2sql and /explore. They accept an analytical pattern graph (node label Analytical_Pattern), read the question from the natural language operator (NLQ_Operator), and connect with DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD plus the database connection node's contentUrl. They return the enriched graph and text-to-SQL metadata. /text2sql4ap omits sql_results from metadata.

  6. Security Layer: This layer intercepts protected requests to perform authentication and authorization. It integrates with an external OIDC provider to validate JWTs and with the DataGEMS Gateway to fetch user-specific permissions.

docs.title: Geospatial Query Flow
docs.text:
1. A user sends a GET /text2geo request with a natural language question about a location.
  2. The Security Layer validates the token and checks for the required user roles.
  3. The service uses Wikidata to identify the most relevant place entity.
  4. An OverpassQL query is generated based on the Wikidata information.
  5. The Overpass API is queried to retrieve geospatial data.
  6. Results are returned, including {lon, lat} points, a [lat, lon] center, GeoJSON, and a bounding box. A missing place is 404. Wikidata or Overpass connectivity failure is 503.

docs.title: Text-to-SQL Query Flow
docs.text:
1. A user sends a POST /text2sql request with a natural language question and database connection information. Coordinate pairs, when present, are disambiguated so the larger magnitude within ±90 is latitude.
  2. The Security Layer validates the token and checks for the required user roles.
  3. The text-to-SQL component generates SQL with DAIL-SQL. TEXT2SQL_FRAMEWORK=opensearch selects the OpenSearch-SQL graph, and TEXT2SQL_LEGACY=true keeps the single-shot pattern path.
  4. For era5land, the prompt includes METEO_DDL and UNIT_CONTRACTS. Few-shot text from in-cluster Qdrant is added only when retrieval is enabled and returns text.
  5. The SQL query is executed against the database in the request.
  6. Results are returned with sql_query and sql_results. If generation or execution fails, the HTTP status can still be 200 and the body "status" is "error".

docs.title: Explore Flow
docs.text:
1. A user sends GET /explore?question=....
  2. text2geo returns coordinates for the place named in the question.
  3. Text-to-SQL runs against DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME_ERA5LAND, and DB_SCHEMA_ERA5LAND.
  4. The response includes sql_query, sql_results, inference_time_s, and db_fetch_time_s.

docs.title: Analytical-pattern-specific flow
docs.text:
1. A user sends POST /text2sql4ap or POST /explore4ap with { "ap": { "nodes", "edges" } }.
  2. The service reads the question from the natural language operator and the relational-database node from the graph.
  3. Database host, port, and name come from the database connection node's contentUrl. The password is the service DB_PASSWORD.
  4. /text2sql4ap generates SQL directly. /explore4ap runs the meteo text-to-SQL agent first.
  5. The enriched graph is returned with metadata. An invalid graph returns 422. DMM or database connection failures return 424.

docs.title: Automations
docs.text: This project leverages GitHub Actions to automate builds, code analysis, security scanning, and documentation deployment. The following sections detail the specific workflows configured for this repository.

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
The creation of a production-ready container image is fully automated by the Dockerfile in the root of the repository. This build process ensures a consistent environment for the application.

  • Stage 1 (Builder): This stage prepares the environment by installing all necessary build-time dependencies, including the full set of Python packages.

  • Stage 2 (Final): This stage constructs the final, lean image by copying only the essential artifacts from the builder stage. It creates a non-root appuser for security, copies the application code, and sets the unicorn server as the entry point.

docs.title: Docker image publishing
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml

This workflow automates the process of building and publishing the service's Docker image to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).

  • Trigger: This workflow runs automatically whenever a new Git tag matching the pattern v* (e.g., v1.0.0, v1.1.0) is pushed to the repository.
  • Process:
    1. Logs into the GitHub Container Registry using a temporary GITHUB_TOKEN.
    2. Uses the docker/metadata-action to automatically generate appropriate Docker tags based on the Git tag.
    3. Builds the Docker image using the Dockerfile.
    4. Pushes the newly built and tagged image to the ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/in-dataset-discovery repository, making it available for deployment.

docs.title: Vulnerability Scanning
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/vulnerability-scan-on-demand.yml

This workflow provides on-demand security scanning of the project's configuration and Docker images using the Trivy security scanner.

  • Trigger: This workflow is run manually from the GitHub Actions UI (workflow_dispatch). It requires an image_tag as input to specify which published Docker image to scan.
  • Process:
    1. Configuration Scan: Scans the Dockerfile and other repository configuration files for potential security misconfigurations.
    2. Image Scan: Pulls the specified Docker image from the GitHub Container Registry and scans its operating system packages and Python libraries for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) with CRITICAL or HIGH severity.
    3. Artifacts: The JSON reports from both the configuration scan and the image scan are uploaded as build artifacts for review.

docs.title: Static Code Analysis
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/code-scan-on-demand.yml

This workflow performs in-depth static code analysis using GitHub CodeQL to find potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and quality issues in the codebase.

  • Trigger: This workflow is run manually from the GitHub Actions UI (workflow_dispatch).
  • Process:
    1. It runs two separate analysis jobs: one for the Python source code and one for the GitHub Actions workflow files themselves.
    2. For each language, it initializes CodeQL using an extended set of security and quality queries.
    3. It performs the analysis and uploads the results directly to the repository's "Security" tab under "Code scanning alerts".

docs.title: Code Metrics
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/code-metrics-on-demand.yml

This workflow generates a report on the complexity and maintainability of the application's Python code using the Radon library.

  • Trigger: This workflow is run manually from the GitHub Actions UI (workflow_dispatch).
  • Process:
    1. Installs the radon Python package.
    2. Runs three types of analysis on the src/app directory:
      • Maintainability Index (MI): A score from 0-100 indicating how easy the code is to maintain.
      • Cyclomatic Complexity (CC): Measures the number of independent paths through the code, indicating its complexity.
      • Raw Lines of Code (LOC): Provides basic code size metrics.
    3. The complete report is compiled into a text file and uploaded as a build artifact named code-metrics-report.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Workflow: .github/workflows/deploy-docs-on-demand.yml

The deployment of this documentation site is automated by a dedicated GitHub Action workflow.

  • Trigger: This workflow is run manually from the GitHub Actions UI (workflow_dispatch).
  • Process: When triggered with a version number (e.g., 1.0.0), the workflow:
    1. Installs mkdocs, mike, and other required tools.
    2. Builds the static HTML site from the markdown source files in the docs/ directory.
    3. Uses the mike tool to commit the built site to the gh-pages branch, organized under the specified version.
    4. Updates the latest alias to point to this newly deployed version, ensuring visitors see the most recent documentation by default.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The In-Dataset Discovery service is configured using a combination of a local configuration file and environment variables.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text:
For local development, the service can be configured using a .env file placed in the root of the repository. The application will automatically load variables from this file on startup.

Warning The .env file is intended for local development only and should be added to your .gitignore file to prevent committing secrets to version control.

docs.title: Example .env file
docs.text:
# .env

# OIDC Authentication
OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/oauth/realms/dev"
OIDC_AUDIENCE="in-dataset-discovery"
GATEWAY_API_URL="https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/gw"

# LLM (default provider is Scayle)
LLM_PROVIDER="scayle"
SCAYLE_BASE_URL="https://chat.scayle.es/api"
SCAYLE_USERNAME="scayle-user"
SCAYLE_PASSWORD="scayle-password"
SCAYLE_MODEL_NAME="Qwen3.8-Flash-Next"

# Optional OpenAI provider (LLM_PROVIDER=openai)
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-your-openai-api-key"
OPENAI_MODEL_NAME="gpt-4o"

# Text-to-SQL
TEXT2SQL_FRAMEWORK="dail"
TEXT2SQL_LEGACY="false"

# ERA5-Land database used by GET /explore
DB_HOST="the_db_host"
DB_PORT="5432"
DB_USER="db_user"
DB_PASSWORD="db_password"
DB_NAME_ERA5LAND="era5land"
DB_SCHEMA_ERA5LAND="public"

# Optional Qdrant few-shot retrieval (era5land only)
RETRIEVAL_ENABLED="false"
QDRANT_URL="http://127.0.0.1:6335"

# LangChain Configuration (optional, for LangSmith)

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Certain configuration variables contain sensitive information and must be handled securely.

docs.title: Identified Secrets
docs.text:
• SCAYLE_PASSWORD: Password for the default Scayle LLM.
  • OPENAI_API_KEY: API key used when LLM_PROVIDER=openai.
  • DB_PASSWORD: Password for GET /explore and the analytical-pattern endpoints.
  • LANGCHAIN_API_KEY: Contains the API key for LangChain services (if used).
  • IdpClientSecret: The client secret used for communication with the identity provider.

POST /text2sql takes database credentials in the request and does not store them. GET /explore and POST /text2sql4ap / POST /explore4ap use the service DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD.

docs.title: Datastores
docs.text: The In-Dataset Discovery service interacts with various data sources and external services to provide its functionality.

docs.title: Overpass API
docs.text:
The service uses the Overpass API to retrieve geospatial data from OpenStreetMap.

  • Technology: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap)
  • Purpose: Supplies OpenStreetMap data for GET /text2geo, and for the text2geo step of GET /explore and POST /explore4ap.
  • Configuration: The Overpass API URL can be configured via the OVERPASS_API_URL environment variable (default: https://overpass-api.de/api/).

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Generated SQL is executed on PostgreSQL through psycopg2.

  • POST /text2sql: Host, port, database, schema, username, and password come from parameters.db_info on each request.
  • GET /explore: Uses the service ERA5-Land settings: DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME_ERA5LAND, and DB_SCHEMA_ERA5LAND.
  • POST /text2sql4ap and POST /explore4ap: These take an analytical pattern graph. Host, port, and database name come from the connection node's contentUrl. Username and password are DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD. The schema is public.

For the era5land database, the table allowlist is landcover_upscaled, landcover_type, and meteo_*. meteo_ssrd.ssrd is stored as J/m².

docs.title: Wikidata
docs.text:
The service uses Wikidata to identify and enrich place information for geospatial queries.

  • Technology: Wikidata REST API
  • Purpose: Identifies places mentioned in natural language queries and retrieves their properties (coordinates, country codes, etc.) for generating OverpassQL queries.

docs.title: Qdrant
docs.text:
Few-shot examples for text-to-SQL are retrieved from in-cluster Qdrant.

  • Purpose: When RETRIEVAL_ENABLED is on and the target database is era5land, a few-shot block from Qdrant is added to the DAIL-SQL prompt if retrieval returns text. Other databases use the live schema only.
  • Configuration: Set QDRANT_URL. The local default is http://127.0.0.1:6335. The in-cluster address is supplied in that variable (for example http://qdrant-service.shared:6333).
  • Startup: If the expected collections are missing, verify_retrieval logs retrieval_degraded and text-to-SQL continues without few-shot text.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The In-Dataset Discovery service is designed for containerized deployment using Docker. This guide provides instructions for building the image, configuring the service, and understanding its dependencies.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: The primary method for deploying the service is via a Docker container. The repository includes a Dockerfile for the build process.

docs.title: Image
docs.text: The image is a single stage based on python:3.12-slim-bookworm. It installs dependencies from pyproject.toml with uv, exposes port 8080, and starts uvicorn src.app.main:app. RETRIEVAL_ENABLED defaults to false in the image. LLM_PROVIDER defaults to scayle.

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
To build and run the container, use the standard Docker commands:

# 1. Build the Docker image
docker build -t in-dataset-discovery .

# 2. Run the container
# Note: You must provide all required environment variables.
docker run -p 8080:8080 \
  --env-file .env \
  --name in-dataset-discovery-service \
  in-dataset-discovery

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: The service requires several external systems and resources to be available at runtime to function correctly.

docs.title: Runtime Dependencies
docs.text:
Scayle chat API: - Description: Default LLM for text-to-SQL and place-name extraction (LLM_PROVIDER=scayle). - Requirement: SCAYLE_BASE_URL, SCAYLE_USERNAME, SCAYLE_PASSWORD, and SCAYLE_MODEL_NAME. OpenAI remains available when LLM_PROVIDER=openai.

Overpass API: - Description: Used for retrieving geospatial data from OpenStreetMap for GET /text2geo and the explore pipeline. - Requirement: Network access to the Overpass API (default: https://overpass-api.de/api/). Can be configured via OVERPASS_API_URL.

Qdrant (optional): - Description: Few-shot examples for era5land text-to-SQL, retrieved from in-cluster Qdrant when RETRIEVAL_ENABLED=true. - Requirement: QDRANT_URL. If the expected collections are missing, startup logs retrieval_degraded and SQL generation continues without few-shot text.

OIDC Provider: - Description: An OpenID Connect compliant identity provider (e.g., Keycloak) is necessary for authenticating users by validating their JWTs (for protected endpoints). - Requirement: The OIDC_ISSUER_URL and OIDC_AUDIENCE must be correctly configured to point to the identity provider.

DataGEMS Gateway (Optional): - Description: The service may communicate with the DataGEMS Gateway API to fetch dataset-level permissions for users. - Requirement: The GATEWAY_API_URL must be configured if gateway integration is needed.

PostgreSQL: - Description: POST /text2sql connects with the request db_info. GET /explore uses the ERA5-Land env vars. POST /text2sql4ap and POST /explore4ap use contentUrl plus DB_USER / DB_PASSWORD. - Requirement: Network access to those databases. The service uses psycopg2.

docs.title: Status & Error Codes
docs.text:
The API uses standard HTTP status codes to indicate the success or failure of a request.

Status Code Meaning Description 200 OK Success The request was successful. POST /text2sql, GET /explore, and the analytical-pattern endpoints can also return 200 with "status": "error" in the body. This soft failure means the call was accepted, but SQL generation or execution did not succeed. The log event is text2sql_soft_failed or meteo_agent_soft_failed. 400 Bad Request Validation Error The request body is malformed or contains invalid data. The response body will contain details about the validation error. 401 Unauthorized Authentication Error The request lacks a valid JWT, the token is expired, or its signature is invalid. 403 Forbidden Authorization Error The user is authenticated but does not have the required role (user or dg_user) to perform the action. 404 Not Found Place Not Found GET /text2geo, and the text2geo step of explore, found no matching place. If LLM authentication fails, the client can receive the same "No place name found" message. The log event is geospatial_place_name_extraction_failed. 422 Unprocessable Entity Validation Error The request is well-formed but missing required fields, or an analytical pattern graph is invalid (missing the natural language operator, the relational-database node, the upstream dataset, or the database connection node contentUrl). 424 Failed Dependency Downstream Service Error A required dependency failed. For POST /text2sql4ap and POST /explore4ap this includes DMM schema fetch failures and PostgreSQL connection failures (DB_USER / DB_PASSWORD against the host in contentUrl). 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected Error An unexpected error occurred on the server while processing the request. This may occur due to agent failures, LLM errors, or other internal issues. 503 Service Unavailable Dependency Unavailable Wikidata or Overpass could not be reached during GET /text2geo or explore. The same status is used when a core component is not ready.

docs.title: Logging & Accounting
docs.text: The service uses structlog for structured, JSON-formatted logging.

docs.title: Log Structure
docs.text:
All log entries are formatted as JSON objects with a consistent structure, including:

  • @t: ISO 8601 timestamp.
  • @mt: The log message (event).
  • @l: The log level (e.g., "Info", "Warning", "Error").
  • DGCorrelationId: A unique ID that ties together all log entries for a single HTTP request.
  • SourceContext: The name of the logger that produced the message.
  • Application: The name of the application (in-dataset-discovery-api).

Additional key-value pairs are added to provide context for specific events.

docs.title: Correlation ID
docs.text:
Every HTTP request is assigned a correlation ID. - If the incoming request includes an x-tracking-correlation header, its value is used. - Otherwise, a new UUID is generated.

This ID is included in every log message generated during the processing of that request and is also returned in the x-tracking-correlation response header. This allows for easy tracing of a request's entire lifecycle through the system and across different services.

docs.title: Request Logging
docs.text:
A middleware automatically logs the end of every HTTP request (except for health checks), capturing:

  • RequestMethod (e.g., GET, POST)
  • RequestPath
  • StatusCode
  • ProcessTimeMS
  • ResponseSize

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text: This document outlines key maintenance tasks for the In-Dataset Discovery Service.

docs.title: Monitoring Service Health
docs.text: Regularly monitor the service health using the /health endpoint to ensure all components are functioning correctly.

docs.title: API Key Management
docs.text:
• Scayle credentials: The default LLM is Scayle (LLM_PROVIDER=scayle). A chat API 401 means the credentials were rejected. Rotate SCAYLE_PASSWORD and restart the pods that should pick it up.
  • OpenAI API Key: Required only when LLM_PROVIDER=openai.
  • LangChain API Key: If using LangSmith, monitor usage and ensure the key is valid.

docs.title: Dependency Updates
docs.text: Regularly update dependencies to: - Fix security vulnerabilities - Get bug fixes and performance improvements - Stay compatible with external services (Overpass API, Scayle, Qdrant, etc.)

docs.title: Log Monitoring
docs.text: Monitor application logs for: - Error patterns that may indicate issues - Performance degradation - Authentication/authorization failures - Downstream service failures (Scayle, Overpass, Wikidata, Qdrant retrieval_degraded, PostgreSQL)

docs.title: Database Connection Management
docs.text: For POST /text2sql, GET /explore, POST /text2sql4ap, and POST /explore4ap: - Monitor database connection performance - POST /text2sql uses credentials from the request. GET /explore and the analytical-pattern endpoints use DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD. - Watch for retrieval_degraded when RETRIEVAL_ENABLED is on and the Qdrant collections are missing.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
1. Scayle errors: A 401 is a credential failure. Timeouts, DNS errors, and 5xx mean the chat API is unreachable. Check SCAYLE_BASE_URL.
  2. Overpass or Wikidata failures: GET /text2geo returns 503 when those services cannot be reached, and 404 when no place is found.
  3. Database connection failures: For POST /text2sql, check the request db_info. For GET /explore and the analytical-pattern endpoints, check DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, and, on those endpoints, contentUrl. Those connection failures return 424.
  4. Authentication Failures: Verify OIDC provider configuration and token validity.
  5. Retrieval: retrieval_degraded at startup means text-to-SQL is running without few-shot examples from in-cluster Qdrant.

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
• Monitor response times for each endpoint
  • Consider caching frequently accessed data (e.g., Wikidata lookups)
  • Optimize LLM prompts to reduce token usage and improve response times
  • Monitor and optimize database query performance for text-to-SQL operations

docs.title: Developer Onboarding Guide

Welcome to the developer guide for the In-Dataset Discovery Service.

This document provides a comprehensive overview of the service's architecture and a step-by-step guide for extending it with new features, agents, and tools.

docs.title: 1. Service Overview
docs.text: The In-Dataset Discovery Service is a FastAPI-based application that provides natural language interfaces for exploring datasets. It uses LLM capabilities to convert user questions into executable queries and agents to orchestrate complex multi-step tasks.

docs.title: Core Principles
docs.text:
The service is built on a few key principles:

  • Modularity: Each component (agents, tools, models) is self-contained and can be extended independently.
  • LLM-Powered: Leverages LLM and LangChain for intelligent query generation and processing.
  • Agent-Based: Uses LangGraph to orchestrate complex workflows that combine multiple tools.
  • Type Safety: Uses Pydantic models for request/response validation and type safety.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
src/
├── app/
│   ├── main.py                 # Process entrypoint (uvicorn target)
│   ├── factory.py              # FastAPI app, router mount, startup
│   ├── routers/
│   │   ├── geospatial.py       # GET /text2geo
│   │   ├── text2sql.py         # POST /text2sql
│   │   ├── explore.py          # GET /explore
│   │   └── ap/
│   │       ├── text2sql4ap.py  # POST /text2sql4ap
│   │       └── explore4ap.py   # POST /explore4ap
│   ├── schemas/                # Pydantic request and response models
│   ├── text2sql4ap_service.py  # AP graph context and SQL enrichment
│   ├── explore4ap_service.py   # Explore run plus AP enrichment
│   ├── config.py
│   └── security.py
├── agents/
│   ├── graph.py                # Meteo text-to-SQL agent (text2geo, then text-to-SQL)
│   ├── text2sql.py             # get_SQL_pattern wrapper
│   └── tools/
│       ├── geospatial_tools.py
│       └── text2sql_tool.py
└── dail_sql/                   # Default SQL generator

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text:
1. Routers (src/app/routers/): HTTP handlers for /text2geo, /text2sql, /explore, /text2sql4ap, and /explore4ap. Request models live in src/app/schemas/.
  2. Meteo text-to-SQL agent (meteo_agent in src/agents/graph.py): LangGraph chain for GET /explore. It runs text2geo, then text-to-SQL.
  3. Text-to-SQL (src/agents/tools/text2sql_tool.py, src/dail_sql/): Default DAIL-SQL generation and PostgreSQL execution. TEXT2SQL_FRAMEWORK=opensearch and TEXT2SQL_LEGACY=true select the other generators.
  4. Analytical-pattern services (src/app/text2sql4ap_service.py, src/app/explore4ap_service.py): Read the question from the natural language operator and the database connection from the analytical pattern graph, then write the SQL back onto the graph.

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text: The API layer (src/app/routers/) handles HTTP requests and responses. src/app/main.py only builds the process. Each endpoint: - Validates input using Pydantic models - Handles authentication (if required) - Calls the appropriate agent or tool - Returns structured responses

docs.title: Agent Layer
docs.text:
Agents are the core processing units that handle specific types of queries:

  • Geospatial Agent: Processes location-based queries
  • Text-to-SQL Agent: Converts questions to SQL queries

docs.title: Tool Layer
docs.text: Tools are reusable functions that agents can invoke. They encapsulate specific operations like: - Querying external APIs (Overpass, Wikidata) - Generating SQL queries - Executing database queries

docs.title: Adding a New API Endpoint
docs.text:
1. Define Request/Response Models in src/app/schemas/:
class MyQueryRequest(BaseModel):
    question: str = Field(..., description="The question to process")

class MyQueryResponse(BaseModel):
    answer: str
    metadata: Dict[str, Any]
  1. Create the Endpoint:
@app.post("/my-endpoint", response_model=MyQueryResponse)
async def my_endpoint(query: MyQueryRequest):
    """Process a query and return results."""
    # Your logic here
    result = process_query(query.question)
    return MyQueryResponse(answer=result, metadata={})
  1. Add Error Handling:
try:
    result = process_query(query.question)
    return MyQueryResponse(answer=result, metadata={})
except Exception as e:
    logger.error("query_failed", error=str(e))
    raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))

docs.title: Adding a New Agent
docs.text:
1. Create Agent File in src/agents/:
# src/agents/my_agent.py
import structlog
from typing import Dict, Any

logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

def my_agent(question: str, log: structlog.BoundLogger) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Process a question using the my_agent."""
    log.info("my_agent_started", question=question)

    # Your agent logic here
    result = process_question(question)

    log.info("my_agent_completed", result=result)
    return result
  1. Add Tools (if needed) in src/agents/tools/:
# src/agents/tools/my_tool.py
def my_tool(param: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """A tool that does something useful."""
    # Tool implementation
    return {"result": "value"}
  1. Integrate with API in a router under src/app/routers/ and include it from src/app/routers/__init__.py:
from src.agents.my_agent import my_agent

@app.get("/my-endpoint")
async def my_endpoint(question: str, log: structlog.BoundLogger = Depends(get_logger)):
    return my_agent(question, log)

docs.title: Adding a New Tool
docs.text:
1. Create Tool File in src/agents/tools/:
# src/agents/tools/my_tool.py
from typing import Dict, Any

def my_tool(param1: str, param2: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Tool description.

    Args:
        param1: Description of param1
        param2: Description of param2

    Returns:
        Dictionary with results
    """
    # Tool implementation
    return {"result": "value"}
  1. Use in Agent:
from src.agents.tools.my_tool import my_tool

def my_agent(question: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    result = my_tool(param1="value", param2=42)
    return result

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
• Follow PEP 8 style guidelines
  • Use type hints for all function parameters and return values
  • Use Pydantic models for data validation
  • Add docstrings to all public functions and classes
  • Use structured logging with structlog
  • Handle errors gracefully and return appropriate HTTP status codes

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Error Handling: Always wrap agent calls in try-except blocks and log errors appropriately.
  2. Logging: Use structured logging with context (user ID, correlation ID, etc.).
  3. Validation: Use Pydantic models for all request/response validation.
  4. Security: Follow the security patterns established in src/app/security.py for protected endpoints.
  5. Testing: Write tests for new features and ensure they pass before submitting PRs.

docs.title: Quality Assurance
docs.text: Quality assurance (QA) combines automated static analysis, vulnerability scanning, and API-level integration testing to ensure the service functions as expected.

docs.title: Code Analysis
docs.text:
We use GitHub CodeQL for static analysis of the source code. This process helps identify potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, and quality issues before they impact production.

  • Technology: GitHub CodeQL
  • Targets: The analysis runs on both the Python source code and the GitHub Actions workflow files themselves.
  • Checks: It uses a set of queries to find common vulnerabilities (e.g., injection flaws, insecure data handling), bugs, and code quality anti-patterns.
  • Execution: The analysis is performed by the on-demand code-scan-on-demand.yml workflow. Results and alerts are available directly in the repository's "Security" tab.

docs.title: Code Metrics
docs.text:
To ensure the long-term maintainability and readability of the code, we use the Radon library to generate code metrics.

  • Technology: Radon
  • Metrics:
    • Maintainability Index (MI): A score from 0-100 indicating how easy the code is to maintain (higher is better).
    • Cyclomatic Complexity (CC): Measures the number of independent paths through the code. A lower score indicates simpler, less complex code.
    • Lines of Code (LOC): Provides raw metrics on the size of the codebase.
  • Execution: The metrics are generated by the on-demand code-metrics-on-demand.yml workflow, which produces a downloadable code-metrics-report.txt artifact.

docs.title: Vulnerability Checks
docs.text:
We use Trivy to scan for known vulnerabilities in our dependencies and container image, ensuring the service is secure from common threats.

  • Technology: Trivy
  • Scans:
    1. Configuration Scan: Scans the Dockerfile and other repository files for security misconfigurations.
    2. Image Scan: Scans the final Docker image for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) with CRITICAL or HIGH severity in its OS packages and Python libraries.
  • Execution: The scan is performed by the on-demand vulnerability-scan-on-demand.yml workflow. It requires an image tag as input and uploads detailed JSON reports as build artifacts.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The service's functionality is validated through API-level integration tests using Postman and its command-line runner, Newman.

  • Test Suite: The test cases are defined in the Postman collection located at tests/in-dataset-discovery-api-tests.postman_collection.json (if available).

  • Test Cases: The suite may include the following tests:

    • Health Check: Verifies that the /health endpoint is available and returns a 200 OK status, indicating the service is healthy.
    • Geospatial Query - Valid Request: Executes a valid geospatial query against GET /text2geo and asserts that the response is successful (200 OK) and has the correct structure.
    • Text-to-SQL Query - Valid Request: Executes a valid text-to-SQL query against POST /text2sql and asserts that the response is successful (200 OK) and contains sql_query and sql_results.

Unit and pipeline coverage for these routes also lives in pytest (tests/test_text2sql_pipeline.py, tests/test_dail_sql_generate.py, tests/test_geospatial_empty_place.py, and the text2sql retrieval tests). Run them with uv run pytest.

docs.title: How to Run Tests
docs.text:
The API tests are designed to be run automatically via a GitHub Actions workflow.

  • Workflow File: .github/workflows/test-on-demand.yml
  • Trigger: The workflow is triggered manually (workflow_dispatch) from the Actions tab in the GitHub repository.
  • Process:
    1. Navigate to the "Actions" tab and select the "Test Scenario (On-Demand)" workflow.
    2. Click "Run workflow". You will be prompted to enter a tag (e.g., main or a specific version like v1.0.0) to test against.
    3. The workflow checks out the specified version of the code.
    4. It then uses the official postman/newman Docker image to execute the test collection.
    5. All necessary environment variables (API base URL, credentials, etc.) are securely injected into the test run from the repository's secrets.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is handled via the OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocols. Every request to a protected endpoint must include a valid JSON Web Token (JWT) in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

The service validates incoming JWTs against the OIDC provider's public keys. The token's signature, issuer, and audience are all verified to ensure its authenticity.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Authorization is role-based. The service checks for specific roles within the validated JWT's claims.

  • Required Roles: All operational endpoints except /health require authentication. That includes GET /text2geo, POST /text2sql, GET /explore, POST /text2sql4ap, POST /explore4ap, and /textQuestionAnswer.

If a user attempts to access an endpoint without the required role, the API will respond with a 403 Forbidden error.

docs.title: Dataset-Level Permissions
docs.text:
In addition to role-based access, the service can enforce dataset-level permissions when integrated with the DataGEMS Gateway.

  • Database Access:
    • POST /text2sql uses the database connection in the request. The caller supplies host, port, database, schema, username, and password. The service does not store those credentials.
    • GET /explore uses the service ERA5-Land settings (DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME_ERA5LAND, DB_SCHEMA_ERA5LAND).
    • POST /text2sql4ap and POST /explore4ap take an analytical pattern graph. Host, port, and database name come from the connection node's contentUrl, and the service authenticates with DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD.
